key_big: A logarithm is an exponent: log_b x = y means b^y = x.
key_sub: log(MN) = log M + log N, log(M/N) = log M − log N, log(M^p) = p log M.
body_html:
How it works

A logarithm is an exponent: logb x = y means by = x. log means base 10, and ln means base e. Logarithms are the inverses of exponential functions.

  • Product: logb(MN) = logb M + logb N
  • Quotient: logb(M/N) = logb M − logb N
  • Power: logb(Mp) = p logb M
  • Change of base: logb x = (log x) ÷ (log b)
Example

Evaluate log2 32.

2 to what power is 32?

25 = 32

Answer: 5

Example

Expand log3(x²y/z).

Add for the top, subtract for the bottom, exponents in front

Answer: 2 log3 x + log3 y − log3 z

Common mistakes

  • Swapping the base and the exponent when converting forms.
  • Writing log(M + N) as log M + log N. The product property is for log(MN).
  • Writing log M ÷ log N for log(M/N). It is a difference.
  • Taking the log of 0 or a negative number. The argument must be positive.

faq.a: A logarithm is an exponent. log_b(x) = y means b^y = x, so log_2(8) = 3 because 2³ = 8.

faq.q: What are the properties of logarithms?
faq.a: Product: log(MN) = log M + log N. Quotient: log(M/N) = log M − log N. Power: log(M^p) = p log M.
log_b(x) = log(x)/log(b) = ln(x)/ln(b). It lets you evaluate any logarithm on a calculator.

faq.q: What is the difference between log and ln?
faq.a: log usually means base 10 (the common logarithm), and ln means base e (the natural logarithm).

items.q: What is the domain of f(x) = log2 (x + 6)?
items.e: You can only take the log of a positive number: x + 6 > 0. x > −6. The graph has a vertical asymptote at x = −6.
Swap x and y: x = 5y. In log form, y = log5 x. f−1(x) = log5 x.
